subject.title: Strict exec timeout semantics: retire askFallback timeout re-admission

question: Should every exec approval that enters pending state become a terminal denial on timeout, including upgraded installations using `askFallback: "full"` or `"allowlist"`?
rationale: Current main and v2026.6.11 deliberately implement and document timeout re-admission, while removal tightens command authorization and may break existing unattended workflows.

options.title: Enforce terminal timeout
options.body: Remove all post-timeout fallback authority and document expiration as permanently denying that pending request.

options.title: Stage a compatibility transition
options.body: Preserve legacy timeout behavior temporarily through a named migration or explicit strict-mode transition before deletion.

options.title: Keep current fallback
options.body: Retain the shipped timeout re-admission contract and revise conflicting documentation instead.

recommendation.title: Enforce terminal timeout
recommendation.body: Remove all post-timeout fallback authority and document expiration as permanently denying that pending request.

likelyOwner.reason: He carried the prerequisite transaction refactor and the timeout-specific replay implementation, giving him the strongest available context for the security and upgrade decision.
